subject: Initial-response latency surge impacting NimbusPay (p95/p99) - escalation
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes — seeing large initial-response latency in hosted API

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a big jump in initial-response latency (first byte / initial token) for our calls to the Redwood hosted API around 10:45 UTC this morning. p95/p99 are worse — the app team says users hit 2–7s delays for the initial response which is breaking our checkout flows. Attached is a small sample of failed requests and timings (nimbus-error-sample.txt).

Can you confirm if this is on your side or something upstream? Our CTO flagged this and asked for an incident timeline and short-term mitigations. We're live in us-east with default CDN routing.

Alex Chen
SRE, NimbusPay Inc.
alex@NimbusPay.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 13:34:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes — seeing large initial-response latency in hosted API

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the sample. I’m escalating this to our SRE/infra team immediately (cc’d).

Quick notes / ask:
- We’ll pull your request IDs from the sample and correlate with our ingress logs.
- Can you share any Datadog links or a time window where you saw the worst p99? That’ll speed things up.
- We’ll aim to provide an interim mitigation within the hour and an RCA within 24h.

I’ve created PagerDuty incident PDINC-7421 and HubSpot HS-32819 for tracking. Monica/Karthik — please triage priority P1. I’ll keep Alex and Nimbus updated.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0148

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes — seeing large initial-response latency in hosted API

Hi all — initial triage results below.

What we see:
- Spike start: ~2026-07-12T10:40:00Z matching Alex’s window.
- Symptom: large increase in TLS handshake durations in our edge logs (SYN->TLS1stByte) for requests routed via EdgeCloudX POPs.
- Impact: first-token latency rises even when model compute time is normal (so downstream runtime not root cause).

Attachments: dd-spike-heatmap.png (screenshot of Datadog showing p95/p99 spike per region).

Next steps (short term):
1) Route NimbusPay’s traffic to a different edge/pool that bypasses the problematic POP (can roll in ~10–15 min).
2) Force keep-alive / session pinning for flows from high-volume clients to reduce handshake rate.
3) Engineering (Karthik) will look for TLS renegotiation or cert/mTLS churn.

Alex — can you confirm whether your calls set Connection: keep-alive and if you use long-lived clients (yes/no)? That will help pick #2.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:18:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes — seeing large initial-response latency in hosted API

Quick engineering summary:

Findings:
- Edge logs show a 3–5x increase in TLS handshake RTT for initial connections coming from the affected POPs; negotiated cipher suites look fine.
- There is a spike in TLS session churn (short TLS session TTL observed) causing frequent full handshakes instead of resumed sessions.
- This coincides with a routing change from CDN partner EdgeCloudX (their control plane rollout at ~10:30Z).

Short-term mitigations we can do now (low risk):
- Re-route NimbusPay traffic to alternate POPs (configured and ready; I can push a route change in 10m).
- Increase our front-door TLS session cache and extend session TTL for affected customers (rolling config change, ~20m to complete).

Medium-term actions:
- Work with EdgeCloudX to pin sessions, add keepalive tuning, and rollback/control-plane fix.
- Add an automated detection that pins live customers to lower-latency POPs when initial-response SLO breaches.

If Nimbus wants an immediate mitigation, we can execute the POP reroute now and then revert once EdgeCloudX confirms fix.

Commands/logs (for ops):
- Route change: redwood route update --customer nimbuspay --bypass-pop edgecloudx-pop-12
- TTL bump: redwood tls-config set --session-ttl 1800 --customer nimbuspay

I’ll stand by to execute with approval.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 18:01:05 -0700
Subject: Executive brief — NimbusPay experiencing first-byte latency regression (p95/p99)

Sean / Marissa — looping you both in. Customer NimbusPay is seeing large p95/p99 regressions in initial-response latency (first-token delays) impacting checkout. Engineering indicates an upstream CDN control-plane rollout caused TLS session churn in certain POPs.

Planned immediate action: route customer traffic around affected POPs and increase session TTLs. Karthik can push changes now if we approve.

Customer impact: user-facing checkout delays; Nimbus is asking for timeline and potential credits.

Requested from leadership: approval to apply POP reroute and offer a one-week service credit if user conversion shows measurable impact. We’ll follow up with a formal RCA within 24 hours.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@NimbusPay.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 20:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive brief — NimbusPay experiencing first-byte latency regression (p95/p99)

Thanks team — please proceed with the POP reroute and session-ttl bump immediately. Prioritize a short customer-facing status update within 30 minutes (Vanessa/Monica).

Also approve: offer NimbusPay a one-week credit and a follow-up customer call with our engineering lead once RCA is ready. Keep me posted.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
